findings.question: Does a statute or binding regulation require government data (or classified government data) to be stored and processed under national or EU jurisdiction? yes = A statute or binding regulation requires it for government data generally; partial = Required only for classified data or only for named sectors; no = A source states there is no such requirement
findings.quote: 3. sa spracúvanie a uloženie údajov uskutočňuje na území členských štátov Európskej únie, zmluvných strán Dohody o Európskom hospodárskom priestore a krajín s primeranou ochranou osobných údajov
findings.quote_english: 3. the processing and storage of data takes place in the territory of EU member states, parties to the EEA Agreement and countries with an adequate level of personal data protection
findings.value: partial
findings.title: Vyhláška MIRRI č. 78/2020 Z. z. o štandardoch pre informačné technológie verejnej správy (consolidated)
findings.note: Binding decree § 45(1)(c) lets public-administration systems use cloud services only if data is processed and stored in the EU/EEA or an adequacy country; adequacy countries lie outside EU jurisdiction, so this is not a strict EU requirement and 'partial' is a judgement call.

review.reason: Vyhláška 78/2020 § 45 is binding, but it covers only cloud services used by public administration systems, and it allows processing in third countries with adequate data protection as well as the EU/EEA; it does not require national or EU jurisdiction, and no source says there is no requirement.
